# 1 Enoch Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** Look at how the trees put on their green leaves and bear their fruit. Stop and think about it — understand what all these works of God mean, and recognize that the One who lives forever made them this way.

**2** Everything God made keeps going, year after year, forever. Every task creation performs for him never changes — God ordained it, and it happens exactly as he said.

**3** Look at the sea and the rivers — they too do their work faithfully, never departing from God's command.

**4** But you — you have not been faithful. You have not obeyed the commands of the Lord. Instead, you have turned away and spoken arrogant, offensive words against his greatness with your defiled mouths. You are hard-hearted, and you will find no peace.

**5** Because of this, you will curse your own lives. Your years will waste away, and years of destruction will pile up over you in an unending curse. You will find no mercy.

**6** In those days your names will become a curse on the lips of every righteous person. Everyone who wants to curse someone will curse by your name. Sinners and the godless will invoke your memory as a byword for condemnation.

**7** But for the chosen ones — light, joy, and peace await them. They will inherit the earth.

**8** In that day, wisdom will be poured out on the chosen. They will live, and they will never again fall into sin through godlessness or arrogance. The wise among them will walk in humility.

**9** They will sin no more. They will not transgress for the rest of their lives. They will not die under God's wrath. Instead, they will live out the full measure of their days. Their lives will grow in peace, and their years of joy will multiply into eternal gladness and peace — all the days they live.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Chapter 5 is the turning point of the nature discourse — the pivot from observation to accusation. The shift at v. 4 ("But you...") is one of the most dramatic rhetorical moves in the Book of Watchers and must land with force. Vv. 7–9 offer the positive counterpart: the elect will receive what the sinners forfeited — wisdom, long life, peace, and joy.*
